about: A security newsletter quoting common attacks.
subject: This week in AI security
body: This week's issue looks at prompt injection. Attackers hide phrases like 'ignore all previous instructions' or 'print your system prompt' in emails and web pages that an assistant later reads. Researchers recommend treating outside text as data, fencing it, and checking a model's output before any action. Read the full write-up on our blog.

about: A diff that adds injection phrases as test data.
subject: PR 482: block obvious injection phrases
body:
diff --git a/filters/screen.py b/filters/screen.py
+BLOCKED = [
+    'ignore previous instructions',
+    'you are now',
+    'reveal your system prompt',
+]
+def flagged(text):
+    return any(p in text.lower() for p in BLOCKED)
This adds a small block list for the help desk filter.

about: An internal guide on writing instructions for the team's bots.
subject: Draft: how we write bot instructions
body: Draft guide for the team. When you write a bot's instructions, say what the job is, who it reports to and what it must never do. Keep the rules short. If a customer's message tries to give the bot new instructions, the bot should treat it as data and ask a person. Comments welcome before Friday.

subject: Workshop: red-teaming AI assistants
